content.title: About
content.content: A pie shell is a ready‑made or semi‑ready layer of dough designed to form the base of sweet and savory pies. It is typically made from wheat flour, butter or margarine, water and a pinch of salt. Thin, crisp and lightly golden, it provides a convenient foundation for any filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional American “pie crust” is often made with cold butter to create a flaky texture.
European “shortcrust” pies use more butter and result in a denser, tender base.
Gluten‑free versions replace wheat flour with rice, corn or almond flour.
A shell can be blind‑baked (without filling) for tarts, or fully covered when the filling is added on top.
Frozen pre‑made shells speed up preparation while still delivering a crisp finish after baking.

items.title: Source of energy
items.content: The crust provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with fuel.

items.title: Contains some protein
items.content: Wheat flour contributes a modest amount of plant‑based protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough supplies thiamine, niacin and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Iron and magnesium
items.content: In small quantities the crust adds minerals that support muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional shells contain wheat, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Shells made with a lot of butter or margarine can be high in calories and saturated fats.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Some ready‑made shells are salty, which should be considered on low‑sodium diets.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Besides gluten, shells may contain dairy if butter is used.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the shell as a base for fruit, berry, custard, meat, vegetable or cheese pies. It can be partially pre‑baked (blind baked) to prevent sogginess, then filled and finished in the oven.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a fresh shell in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Frozen shells keep for about 3 months; thaw them in the fridge before use.
